about: Hand-written rotation guides for the hunter's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: Beast Mastery in a raid is **Auto Shot** and your pet with a short list on top: keep **Serpent Sting** ticking, fire **Arcane Shot** and **Aimed Shot** each time their cooldowns end, and send **Bestial Wrath** whenever it is ready.
why: **Serpent Sting** comes first so it never drops: on the training dummy it is about 15% of this build's damage, 20% more with **Improved Stings**. Recast it only as it runs out, since a new sting replaces the old one and its last ticks; the full-raid rotation recasts it only while you have 30% mana or more.

**Arcane Shot** goes out every time its cooldown ends: 5.4 seconds with 2 points in **Improved Arcane Shot**, about 33 times in a 3-minute fight. **Summon Hawk** shares that cooldown, and the full-raid rotation gives all of it to **Arcane Shot**, so the build's **Summon Hawk** point is never cast.

**Rapid Fire** (40% faster attacks for 15 seconds, 5-minute cooldown) goes once a fight, at the pull. The full rotation presses it just before an **Auto Shot** with **Aimed Shot** about to come off cooldown, so the next **Aimed Shot** is cast under it.

**Aimed Shot** is last on the list but it is not a spam filler: it goes out almost every time it can, a 2-second cast and then its 6-second cooldown, about 23 times a fight. The instants above it cost only a global cooldown.

**Bestial Wrath** (+50% pet damage for 18 seconds) goes at the pull and on every 2-minute cooldown, twice a fight. **Intimidation** is in the build only because **Bestial Wrath** requires it; the full-raid list never presses it.

Your pet is about a quarter of your damage on the training dummy. It takes 10% of your attack power and all of your crit (this project's model of Forever's pet scaling), so **Ferocity** and **Frenzy** keep it critting and attacking faster, and **Focused Fire** adds 2% to you both while it is out.
caveats: Mana: the list assumes a full raid with Blessing of Wisdom and Mana Spring. With only your own buffs the simulator's best rotation never casts **Aimed Shot** (310 mana) and keeps **Arcane Shot** going above 10% mana, so **Aimed Shot** is the first thing to drop when you run low.

Keep the pet alive with **Mend Pet**: Forever pets take no stat buffs from players, and a dead pet takes **Focused Fire** with it. A faster pet does more damage as modelled here (a 1.2-second cat over a 2.0-second pet; players have measured this only at levels 20 and 30).
Moving: **Auto Shot** and **Aimed Shot** stop while you move; **Arcane Shot** and **Serpent Sting** are instant, so keep pressing them.
The simulator starts **Aimed Shot** 2.5 seconds before the pull so it lands as the fight begins; in a real raid, start it once your tank has the boss.

Watch your ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 gives +143 ranged attack power (rank 3 +98), **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75; if your build has it) and **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 +120 (rank 6 +110). Cast the highest rank you have.
diverge: Two or more targets close together: **Multi-Shot** instead of **Aimed Shot** on their shared cooldown, since it hits up to 3 targets for weapon damage each while **Aimed Shot** adds 350 to one. For a pack, **Volley**: a 6-second channel with no cooldown in Forever, which holds **Auto Shot** while you channel.
In the last few seconds, skip the **Serpent Sting** refresh: its damage comes over 15 seconds. The simulator's other hunter rotations stop refreshing it 3 to 6 seconds before the end.
Inside 8 yards your shots and **Auto Shot** stop. Step back out; if you cannot, **Summon Hawk** still works, as it has no minimum range.

leveling.plan: Beast Mastery levels with the cat as the tank: it holds the mob while **Auto Shot**, **Serpent Sting** and **Aimed Shot** kill it from range. The build puts its first 31 points into the pet (**Deadly Aspects** from level 10, **Unleashed Fury** at 20, **Ferocity** at 25, **Bestial Wrath** at 40) and then adds Marksmanship's crit and cheaper shots. Your job is to keep the mob on the pet and to spend mana only where it shortens the fight.
why: Send the pet first, then **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting**. In the fight lab the cat Growls every 5 seconds and keeps the mob until your threat passes 130% of its own, so two cheap openers give it a head start; the lab casts the mark only while the mob has more than 30% of its health and the sting while it has more than 40%.

**Aimed Shot** (from level 20) is your only cooldown shot on a single mob, cast while the mob has more than a quarter of its health. The fight lab's tuned rules (2026-11-03) never cast **Multi-Shot** (it shares the cooldown) or **Arcane Shot**: their mana is worth more as fewer drinks between pulls. This build has no **Summon Hawk** point (the rules switch the hawk off as well).

The pet talents come first: **Deadly Aspects** (levels 10-14), **Unleashed Fury** (20-24), **Ferocity** (25-29) and **Bestial Discipline** (30-31, half your mana regeneration keeps running while you cast). In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent) **Unleashed Fury** is worth about 1.0 second, **Bestial Discipline** about 0.9, **Efficiency** (46-50) about 0.85 and **Ferocity** about 0.7: the build's four most valuable talents. **Trueshot Aura** (56) is a buff you cast in Forever: keep it on.

**Rapid Fire** (26) at the start of a fight whenever it is ready (a 5-minute cooldown here: no **Rapid Killing**); **Intimidation** (34) and **Bestial Wrath** (40) likewise, the pet's stun and rage at the pull. **Bestial Wrath** has a 2-minute cooldown, so it goes on the first pull and then again every few pulls.

At 60 the pet is about a third of your damage (34% in the fight lab) and your shots most of the rest. The bow cannot fire within 8 yards: if the mob ends up next to you while the pet holds it, step back rather than melee.

**Mend Pet** when the pet drops below about a third while it holds the mob, and between fights below half. A dead pet costs a **Revive Pet** before the next pull and your **Focused Fire** bonus until then. Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules change neither.
caveats: **Intimidation** is the point that opens **Bestial Wrath**: cast on its own it measured slightly slower in the fight lab (about 0.2 seconds a kill), and **Bestial Wrath** itself is worth about 0.2. **Endurance Training**, **Bestial Swiftness** and **Spirit Bond** measured nothing at 60 (a sturdier, faster, self-healing pet; the lab's pet rarely dies).

A mob that turns on you: **Feign Death** sends it back to the pet; while it is on cooldown, **Mongoose Bite** after a dodge, **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip** until the pet's Growl takes the mob back.
Several mobs at once: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (from level 40; a 6-second channel with no cooldown in Forever) are your area damage.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 57-60, 4 points) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 gives +120 ranged attack power (rank 6 +110), **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 +143 (rank 3 +98) and **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75). Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: When the mob is nearly dead, stop spending mana: **Auto Shot** and the pet finish it, and you start the next pull fuller.
If the pet dies mid-fight, finish the mob with **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip** (or **Feign Death** if it is going badly), and revive the pet before the next pull.

raid.plan: Marksmanship plays without a pet: **Lone Wolf** adds 20% to everything you do while no pet is out. **Auto Shot** is about half your damage; **Aimed Shot**, **Arcane Shot** and **Sniper Shot** go out as soon as their cooldowns allow, biggest first.
why: Before the pull: **Dismiss Pet**, cast **Trueshot Aura** (in Forever a buff you cast, 30 minutes for your party and raid) and **Aspect of the Hawk**, and track the boss's creature type, since **Improved Tracking** adds 5% only against the tracked type. In the simulator **Lone Wolf** is about 16% of this build's damage, more than any other talent.

**Aimed Shot** comes first: it is your biggest regular hit (weapon damage plus 350, 10% more with **Barrage**), and its 6-second cooldown starts only when the 2-second cast ends, so any delay pushes every later cast back. The simulator measured about 4% more damage with it at the top.

**Rapid Fire** gives 40% faster attacks for 15 seconds; **Rapid Killing** cuts its cooldown to 3 minutes, so it comes once in a 3-minute fight, at the pull. The full rotation presses it right before an **Auto Shot**.

**Serpent Sting**: recast it in its last second, but not when **Aimed Shot** is half a second from ready. Each sting also starts **Rapid Recuperation** (a quarter of your mana regeneration keeps going while you cast, for 15 seconds), so it pays back some mana.
**Arcane Shot** comes back every 4.5 seconds with 5 points in **Improved Arcane Shot**: about 33 casts a fight, more than any other button, filling the gaps between **Aimed Shot** casts.

**Sniper Shot** hits hardest (weapon damage plus 590) but takes 4 seconds, so it goes last: start it only when **Aimed Shot** is at least a second from ready. It is not a true filler: it has a 15-second cooldown and comes about 9 times a fight, and between casts **Auto Shot** does the work.
caveats: **Multi-Shot** is on the list but shares **Aimed Shot**'s cooldown, so on one target it almost never comes up (the simulator cast it about once in five fights). It is there for groups of targets.

Mana is tight even in a full raid: the simulator's hunter uses two mana potions a fight and still runs dry for a few seconds. With only your own buffs its rotation never casts **Sniper Shot** (365 mana) and casts **Aimed Shot** only above 10% mana.

Moving: **Auto Shot**, **Aimed Shot** and **Sniper Shot** need you to stand still, while **Arcane Shot** and **Serpent Sting** are instant. Do not start a 4-second **Sniper Shot** when you know you must move.
**Rapid Killing**'s other half (a kill makes your next Shot within 20 seconds hit 20% harder) never happens on a boss; on trash, let the next pull's first **Aimed Shot** spend it.

Watch your ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 gives +143 ranged attack power (rank 3 +98), **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75; if your build has it) and **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 +120 (rank 6 +110). Cast the highest rank you have.
diverge: Two or three targets close together: **Multi-Shot** instead of **Aimed Shot** (same cooldown, up to 3 targets for weapon damage each). For a pack, **Volley**: a 6-second channel with no cooldown in Forever.
In the last seconds, skip the **Serpent Sting** refresh and do not start a **Sniper Shot** that will not finish; **Arcane Shot** instead.
With a pet out **Lone Wolf** does nothing: if you want the pet, take the pet build linked above, whose rotation puts **Arcane Shot** first.

leveling.plan: Marksmanship levels with the pet tanking, but more of the damage is your own: **Aimed Shot** on its cooldown, **Serpent Sting** on every mob, **Arcane Shot** to finish once the mob is below 35% of its health, **Trueshot Aura** always on and **Auto Shot** in between. The build spends its first 30 points on Marksmanship (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**, **Efficiency**) and the other 21 on the pet.
why: Send the pet first, then **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** while the mob is healthy (the fight lab: above 30% and 40% of its health). The cat holds the mob until your threat passes 130% of its own.

**Aimed Shot** gets the cooldown it shares with **Multi-Shot**, while the mob has more than a quarter of its health. The tuned rules (2026-11-03) never cast **Multi-Shot** on a single mob, and cast **Arcane Shot** only once the mob is below 35% of its health: earlier, its mana did less than the next **Aimed Shot** and **Serpent Sting**. In the band between a quarter and 35% of the mob's health both are allowed, and there the fight lab fires **Arcane Shot** before **Aimed Shot**, as the list above puts it.

**Lethal Attacks** and **Careful Aim** (levels 10-19) first, **Improved Stings** (20-22), then **Rapid Killing** (23-24), which cuts **Rapid Fire** to 3 minutes. **Trueshot Aura** (25) is a buff you cast in Forever: keep it on. **Efficiency** (26-29 and 31) is the build's most valuable talent at 60: about a second a kill in the fight lab's removal runs, ahead of **Unleashed Fury** (50-54, 0.9) and **Lethal Attacks** (0.6).
From level 40 the points go to the pet: **Deadly Aspects**, **Focused Fire**, **Endurance Training**, then **Unleashed Fury** and **Ferocity** (50-59) and **Bestial Discipline** (60).
Your shots and stings are 72% of the damage at 60 in the fight lab, the cat most of the rest. **Auto Shot** cannot fire within 8 yards: step back out rather than melee while the pet holds the mob.
Drink below 15% mana rather than at 35%: it measured slightly faster (under 1% per kill). **Feign Death** only while the mob has more than 35% of its health; below that, finish it.
caveats: **Rapid Recuperation** (30, one point; it needs both points of **Rapid Killing**): **Serpent Sting** lets a quarter of your mana regeneration continue while casting for 15 seconds, half after you spend a **Rapid Killing**. It measured about 0.4 seconds a kill at 60. **Barrage** (32-34) adds 15% to **Aimed Shot**, **Multi-Shot** and **Volley**: little on one mob (0.16 seconds), more on several.

**Rapid Killing** also makes your next Shot within 20 seconds of a kill hit 20% harder; the fight lab leaves that half out, so let the next pull's first **Aimed Shot** spend it. Without the bonus the talent measured almost nothing: its points open **Rapid Recuperation**.
**Endurance Training** and **Improved Aspect of the Monkey** (49) measured nothing at 60 in the fight lab: they fill tiers. **Ranged Weapon Specialization** (35-39) is 5% more damage with your bow.

A mob that turns on you while it still has more than 35% of its health: **Feign Death** sends it back to the pet; while it is on cooldown, **Mongoose Bite** after a dodge, **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip**.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 gives +120 ranged attack power (rank 6 +110), **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 +143 (rank 3 +98) and **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75). Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: Several mobs: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (no cooldown in Forever) instead of single-target shots.
A mob on you while the pet is down: slow it with **Wing Clip** or **Concussive Shot**, step back past 8 yards and shoot.

raid.plan: Melee Survival fights at the boss with two one-handers and no pet. **Raptor Strike** replaces a swing every 6 seconds, **Mongoose Bite** goes whenever it lights up, **Strider Kick** and **Immolation Trap** go on cooldown, and **Wing Clip** fills every other global cooldown.
why: **Hunter's Mark** before the pull is for **Expose Prey**: each of your hits on a marked target has a 10% chance to light up **Mongoose Bite** for 10 seconds. Otherwise **Mongoose Bite** lights up only after you dodge (not the boss), and in a raid the boss hits your tank, so nearly all your bites, about 39 a fight, come from **Expose Prey**. The mark lasts 2 minutes: put it back when it drops.

**Aspect of the Beast** adds 110 melee attack power, and with **Deadly Aspects** each melee auto attack has a 10% chance to speed your swings by 30% for 12 seconds. **Rapid Fire** speeds up melee too in Forever (40% for 15 seconds): press it at the pull.
**Raptor Strike** is first and never waits: it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown, so queue it every time its 6-second cooldown ends.

**Mongoose Bite** next, as soon as it lights up: weapon damage plus 57, and **Lacerating Strikes** adds a bleed worth 40% of the bite over 21 seconds. Using it at once frees its 5-second cooldown for the next one.

**Strider Kick** (full weapon damage, 8-second cooldown) and **Immolation Trap** go on cooldown. Traps work in combat in Forever but land at your own feet, so standing at the boss puts the trap under it: 690 Fire damage over 15 seconds, 30% more with **Clever Traps**, every 18 seconds with **Survivalist's Discipline**.

**Wing Clip** is the filler. Its own hit is small (50 damage), but every hit on your marked target is another chance at **Mongoose Bite**, and the simulator measured about 10% more damage in a full raid with **Wing Clip** in every empty global cooldown.
caveats: No pet: **Lone Wolf**'s 20% needs no active pet, so **Dismiss Pet** before the pull. Track the boss's creature type too: **Improved Tracking** adds 5% only against the type you are tracking.

Mana: **Resourcefulness** cuts the cost of traps and melee abilities by 60%, and in a full raid that is enough. With only your own buffs the hunter runs short; then spend the mana on **Mongoose Bite**, **Strider Kick** and the trap before **Wing Clip**.
Blizzard's notes say **Expose Prey** works on the target of your own **Hunter's Mark**. With several hunters in the raid, make sure the mark on the boss is yours (the simulator accepts any).

**Explosive Trap** and **Immolation Trap** share the fire-trap cooldown. With a raid's mana the list spends it on **Explosive Trap** (about 9 a fight in the simulator, **Immolation Trap** about once); below 60% mana, **Immolation Trap** takes it.

Watch your ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 gives +143 ranged attack power (rank 3 +98) and **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 +110 melee attack power (rank 3 +90). Cast the highest rank you have.
diverge: Adds around you: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards.
When you must leave the boss, make **Strider Kick** your last hit: it adds 30% movement speed for 3 seconds.
If you pull threat, **Feign Death** (30-second cooldown; **Survival Tactics** makes it more likely to land).
In the last few seconds, skip a fresh **Immolation Trap**: its damage comes over 15 seconds.

leveling.plan: Melee Survival levels with the pet as the tank: you walk in behind it and fight beside it with two one-handers. **Raptor Strike** finishes the mob, **Mongoose Bite** comes when it lights up, **Immolation Trap** burns the longer fights, **Lacerate** adds a bleed from level 30, and white swings do the rest. The build puts 30 points into Survival, 16 into Marksmanship (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**) and 5 into **Deadly Aspects**.
why: **Serpent Sting** as the mob comes in: the lab casts it from range, while the mob is still 8 yards or more away and has more than 40% of its health, then you walk in behind the pet. The tuned rules (2026-11-03) never cast **Hunter's Mark** for a melee hunter: it measured slower even with **Expose Prey**.

**Raptor Strike** is kept for the finish: the tuned rules cast it only once the mob is below 20% of its health. It replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown, so queue it first when it is up. Held back, its mana buys more in the sting, the trap and **Lacerate**.

**Immolation Trap** goes at your feet beside the mob (traps work in combat in Forever but land where you stand), while the mob has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds). **Resourcefulness** (levels 30 and 32) cuts the cost of traps and melee abilities by 60%.
**Lacerate** (trained at 30) only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more: cast freely, its mana cost more time than its bleed saved.

**Mongoose Bite** lights up after you dodge, so **Aspect of the Monkey** (its dodges) until level 30; then **Aspect of the Beast**: melee attack power, and with **Deadly Aspects** (50-54) a chance per melee auto attack for 30% faster swings for 12 seconds. **Deflection** raises your parry.

In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent), **Resourcefulness** is worth about 2.1 seconds, **Survivalist's Discipline** (33-34, the trap every 18 seconds) 1.4, **Clever Traps** 0.7, **Lethal Attacks** 0.6, **Surefooted** 0.5 and **Improved Tracking** 0.5: the build's most valuable talents. Melee, Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite, Lacerate, Wing Clip and the pet are 58% of the damage at 60.
Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules change neither.
caveats: This build does not take **Counterattack**, nor **Deterrence**, nor **Strider Kick**, so the list above leaves their lines out; **Mongoose Bite** still goes whenever a dodge lights it up. **Expose Prey** (31) only works on a mob you marked with **Hunter's Mark**, and the rules never cast the mark: it measured nothing.
The pet is still your tank: **Mend Pet** below about a third in the fight and below half between fights, and let it build threat before you hit hard.

The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (the spec's rule: at least half at 60; this build reaches 58%). The sting and the trap are not counted, which is why the rotation does not lean on them harder.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.
**Rapid Killing** (58-59) and **Mortal Shots** (60) are ranged talents that measured nothing here: the last points of the tree.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
If the pet dies mid-fight, finish the mob and step back, or **Feign Death** if it is going badly; revive the pet before the next pull.

**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: Several mobs: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (no cooldown in Forever) instead of single-target shots.
If the pet dies, finish the mob in melee or **Feign Death**, and revive it before the next pull. When a mob is nearly dead, stop spending mana and let **Auto Shot** and the pet finish it.

leveling.plan: The split melee build plays the melee Survival list: walk in behind the pet, trap at your feet and fight beside it. Its Marksmanship points buy crit and attack power (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**), and **Survivalist's Discipline** brings the trap back sooner.
why: **Serpent Sting** as the mob runs in, from range, then walk in behind the pet: the fight lab's tuned rules (2026-11-03) cast it while the mob has more than 40% of its health, and never cast **Hunter's Mark** for a melee hunter.
**Immolation Trap** at your feet beside the mob, while it has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds). **Survivalist's Discipline** cuts its cooldown from 30 to 18 seconds.

**Raptor Strike** once the mob is below 20% of its health (it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown). **Lacerate** only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more.

**Mongoose Bite** when it lights up after you dodge. **Expose Prey** would also light it up from your hits on a marked mob, but the tuned rules never cast **Hunter's Mark**. **Counterattack** after you parry; **Deflection** raises your parry.

**Deterrence** below 40% health while the mob has more than 30% of its health: +25% dodge and parry for 10 seconds, every 3 minutes with **Survivalist's Discipline**, and those dodges and parries light up **Mongoose Bite** and **Counterattack**.
Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules change neither.
caveats: The tuned rules cast **Raptor Strike** and **Strider Kick** only once the mob is below 20% of its health, and **Lacerate** only above half its health with 80% of your mana. The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (at least half at 60).
**Aspect of the Monkey** until level 30, then **Aspect of the Beast** for its melee attack power; **Deadly Aspects** adds its swing-speed chance to **Aspect of the Beast**.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds damage only against the creature type you are tracking: keep tracking set to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
If the pet dies, **Deterrence** and finish the mob, or **Feign Death** if it is going badly; revive the pet before the next pull.

raid.plan: Beast-Survival plays the melee Survival list with **Summon Hawk** added: no pet, so **Lone Wolf**'s 20% stays on, and up to two hawks attack the boss beside you.
why: **Raptor Strike** first whenever it is ready: it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown. Then **Mongoose Bite** when it lights up and **Strider Kick** on its 8-second cooldown.

**Summon Hawk** next, about 27 times in a 3-minute fight: a dive bomb plus 5% of your ranged attack power, then a hawk that attacks for 18 seconds. Two can be out at once and a new one replaces the one closest to leaving; **Unleashed Fury** makes them hit 15% harder. The simulator measured about 15% more damage in a full raid once the hawk joined the melee rotation, and it counts hawks as guardians, not pets, so **Lone Wolf** stays on while they fly.

**Hunter's Mark** before the pull is for **Expose Prey**: each hit on a marked target has a 10% chance to light up **Mongoose Bite** for 10 seconds, and in a raid you rarely dodge, the bite's only other trigger. Recast the mark when its 2 minutes run out.

**Immolation Trap** at your feet under the boss every 24 seconds (one point in **Survivalist's Discipline**), 30% stronger with **Clever Traps**. **Wing Clip** fills the global cooldowns left over, for its small hit and another chance at **Mongoose Bite**.
caveats: Mana: this build has no **Resourcefulness**, and each hawk costs 190 mana. In a full raid the simulator needs one mana potion a fight; with only your own buffs it ran out of mana and fell about a quarter behind the Survival builds on the training dummy. Without Blessing of Wisdom or Mana Spring, play Survival.
The build rests on the simulator's reading that a hawk is not a pet: if the game counts hawks as pets, **Lone Wolf** turns off while they are out. Check it at launch.
No pet: **Dismiss Pet** before the pull. Track the boss's creature type: **Improved Tracking** adds 5% only against the tracked type.

Watch your ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 gives +143 ranged attack power (rank 3 +98) and **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 +110 melee attack power (rank 3 +90). Cast the highest rank you have.
diverge: Adds around you: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; they share the fire-trap cooldown.
Pulled off the boss by a mechanic: **Summon Hawk** reaches 35 yards, so keep the hawks coming, and make **Strider Kick** your last hit before you run (30% movement speed for 3 seconds).
Short on mana: let **Wing Clip** go first; its own hit is your least damage per point of mana.

leveling.plan: Beast-Survival levels on **Immolation Trap** and a strong pet: the cat tanks and hits hard, you walk in behind it, drop a trap at your feet and fight beside it with **Raptor Strike** and your white swings. Survival comes first (levels 10-33), then the pet.
why: **Immolation Trap** is the heart of the build: **Clever Traps** (levels 23-24) adds to it, **Survival Tactics** (29) helps it hit, and **Survivalist's Discipline** (32-33) brings it back every 18 seconds. In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent), **Resourcefulness** (levels 30-31: cheaper traps and strikes) was worth about 1.9 seconds and **Survivalist's Discipline** 1.4, the build's most valuable talents; **Clever Traps** 0.7 and **Bestial Discipline** 0.5 come next.
Set the trap at your feet beside the mob (traps work in combat in Forever but land where you stand), only while the mob has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds).

**Serpent Sting** as the mob runs in, from range (more than 8 yards away, mob above 40% of its health), then walk in behind the pet. **Raptor Strike** only once the mob is below 20% of its health: the tuned rules (2026-11-03) hold it for the finish (it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown). **Mongoose Bite** lights up only after you dodge, which is rare while the pet holds the mob: the fight lab casts it almost never (none at 60). **Lacerate** (from level 30) only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more.

From level 34 the points go to **Lethal Attacks** and then Beast Mastery: **Deadly Aspects** for your swings (39-43), then the pet: **Focused Fire**, **Endurance Training**, **Unleashed Fury** (49-51), **Ferocity** (54-58) and **Bestial Discipline** (59-60). The cat's swings and Claw are a large part of the damage at 60: send it first and let it hold the mob.

The tuned rules never cast **Hunter's Mark**, and the build has no **Expose Prey**. **Aspect of the Monkey** until level 30, then **Aspect of the Beast**. Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health.
caveats: This build takes no **Strider Kick**, nor **Counterattack**, nor **Deterrence**, nor **Expose Prey**: the list above leaves their lines out. Between traps your global cooldown is mostly free, and white swings and the pet do most of the damage.

The list is shared with Survival: the tuned rules hold **Raptor Strike** (this build lacks **Strider Kick**) for the last 20% of the mob's health. The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (at least half at 60; this build reaches 59%).

**Savage Strikes** (15-16), **Deflection** (17-18) and **Survivalist** (19) measured almost nothing at 60 in the fight lab: they fill the tree's first rows. **Improved Aspect of the Monkey** (52-53) measured nothing.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
Low on health: **Mend Pet** keeps your tank up, and **Feign Death** drops the mob back on the pet if it turns on you.
